title: Dedicated-capacity-pricing-pilot-announce-draft
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for the internal announcement + manager Q&A for the Dedicated Capacity pricing pilot we intend to roll out to a small set of customers next week. This is rough — please add gaps and tone down legal phrasing.

Audience:
- All Redwood employees (primary: sales, customer success, eng-support, product)
- Managers who will field questions from customers and internal stakeholders

Top-line message (one sentence):
We’re starting a limited pricing pilot for Redwood Dedicated to validate a simplified instance-based pricing model that improves cost predictability for large customers while testing autoscaling economics.

Why this pilot now (bullet points):
- Dedicated demand heatmap: several customers asked for predictable monthly bills (not per-token variability).
- We have stable telemetry on stable workloads to simulate the unit economics for 3 months.
- Product aim: reduce churn at enterprise scale and make Dedicated easier to sell to platform teams.

What we’re testing (short):
- Offer: fixed monthly instance pricing tiers (small/medium/large) with optional burst add-on.
- Eligibility: invite-only (ten customers) with existing Dedicated contracts, committed for 90 days.
- Metrics: churn propensity, average cost per 1k tokens at 95th percentile, latency SLO compliance, CS satisfaction NPS.

Rollout timeline (high-level):
- Week 0 (internal): announce pilot to internal teams + training (this doc)
- Week 1: invite acceptances + provisioning automation test for 2 Canary customers
- Weeks 2–6: onboard rest of pilot cohort, daily metrics dashboard + weekly review
- Week 7: interim findings, decide widen/stop/iterate

Manager talking points (for customer conversations):
- Lead with the benefit: "This pilot is to give your team predictable, committed capacity and simpler monthly invoicing while we jointly tune autoscale behavior to match your load."
- Reassure on quality: "No model quality changes — this is purely billing & capacity shaping; your pinned model versions remain the same."
- Failure modes and protections: "You can opt-back to your prior contract at any time during the pilot window; we have automatic rollback if latency SLOs degrade beyond threshold."

Anticipated internal questions + suggested responses (Q&A):
Q: Why invite-only?
A: We want a controlled sample to validate telemetry, and to avoid confusing broader billing. Invite cohort is selected to represent three workload archetypes: steady, spiky, and bursty.

Q: Will this increase our revenue short-term?
A: Not necessarily — pricing is not aimed at immediate uplift but at reducing churn and sales friction. We expect revenue-neutral to slightly positive in cohort; primary KPI is reduction in billing disputes and faster procurement cycles.

Q: What if a customer’s usage is much lower than their instance tier?
A: We will surface utilization reports weekly; customers can switch tiers monthly during the pilot with a pro-rated adjustment. We will capture any gross oversubscription risk and discuss credits if our modeling was off.

Q: How will this affect Dedicated SLAs and support?
A: SLAs remain the same. For pilot customers we have a dedicated CS + SRE on-call rotation and a 24h prioritization window for anything impacting provisioning or latency.

Q: Is this compatible with private deployments?
A: Pilot is initially for hosted Dedicated pools only. We will evaluate private/VPC after telemetry looks sane.

Open questions we still need to resolve (notes to self):
- Final legal language for opt-in and opt-out (Priya to lock with legal by EOD Thu).
- Billing system pro-rate implementation details (Finance to confirm).
- Clear internal dashboard view for per-customer utilization (Elliot + Observability).
- Customer communications template for formal invite (Maya drafting).

Support playbook (short):
- Slack channel: #pilot-dedicated-pricing (use for urgent escalation; include customer tag and provisioning ID)
- CS triage: level-1 handles billing inquiries; escalate to SRE if latency or provisioning failures occur
- Incident comms: for any SLO breach, notify customer within 30 minutes, include remediation ETA and temporary mitigations (fallback routes or additional instances)

Manager email template (for reps to send to invited customers):
"Hi [Customer],
We’d like to invite you to participate in a limited pilot of our new Dedicated instance pricing aimed at simplifying billing and providing predictable capacity. The pilot is invite-only, 90-day, and includes a dedicated onboarding runbook plus enhanced support. If interested, reply and we’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff to review technical details and next steps.
Thanks,
[name]"

Internal quick checklist before public-internal announcement (tick when done):
- [ ] Legal opt-in text finalized
- [ ] Finance confirms pro-rate behavior
- [ ] Observability dashboard prototype live for Canary customers
- [ ] CS playbook doc linked in channel
- [ ] Training session scheduled for sales + CS (30m)

What success looks like (pilot decision criteria):
- Reduced billing disputes for pilot cohort by >= 50% vs prior quarter
- No sustained SLO regressions (>5% customers with >threshold breaches)
- 80% of pilot customers report the pricing model made procurement easier in follow-up survey

Notes / rough edits (freeform):
- Might want to avoid the word "lock-in" in public comms — use "commitment" and emphasize monthly switch window.
- Consider offering a one-time implementation credit to offset migration noise.
- Keep the invite email short; detailed T&Cs in the kickoff doc, not the initial outreach.

Next steps for this doc (who does what):
- Priya: legal language + final manager one-pager (due 2026-03-13)
- Elliot: dashboard links + telemetry queries (due 2026-03-15)
- Maya: customer invite email + kickoff slide deck (due 2026-03-13)
- Arthur (me): consolidate feedback, schedule internal training (target 2026-03-14)

If you edit this doc, prefix your note with initials and date. Keep changes terse — this will become the single source for manager comms for the pilot.

End of scratchpad.
